summary: # Advanced Pinching | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction My name's Phoebe, and I have some great updates to share with you regarding selection and simulation, specifically how you can select better and more advanced options within Clo in our updated version of 2025.0. So, let's dive in and have some fun while we learn! ## Accessing Advanced Pinching First, let's discuss where to find this tool. The advanced pinching option can only be accessed when simulation is turned on. You can enable simulation in either CPU or GPU mode. I recommend using GPU for optimal performance. If you're on a machine that lacks GPU capabilities, just use CPU as a reminder. To activate simulation, I'll hit my spacebar. Once simulation is on, I can access the new selection option. You can find this under the tool menu; remember, if you see a small triangle next to a tool, it indicates that there are more options available. Click and hold to reveal these options. ### Activation Steps 1. Turn on simulation (CPU or GPU). 2. Access the tool menu. 3. Click and hold to select **Advanced Pinching**. If I turn off simulation, the options will disappear. However, turning simulation back on will automatically show the advanced pinching option again. ## Understanding Advanced Pinching Settings When you hover over your pattern pieces or garments, you'll see some circles indicating what you're selecting. Let's break down the advanced pinch settings: ### Fall Off Shape - **Bump vs. Linear**: - The "bump" option refers to a graphical representation of selection, which can be displayed as either bump or linear. The graph will change depending on your selection. ### Fall Off Distance and Power - **Fall Off Distance**: This setting relates to the outer circle. A smaller distance results in a smaller selection area, while a larger distance increases the selection area. - **Fall Off Power**: This setting relates to the inner circle, which is the most powerful selection area. If you want a strong selection, lower the fall-off power. If you prefer a softer selection, increase the fall-off power. ### Visual Indicators The green area indicates what is currently selected. Adjusting the fall-off settings allows you to control how much of the garment moves versus how much remains unaffected. ## Selection Techniques ### Distance Measurement - **Surface vs. Straight**: - **Surface**: This option follows the surface of the pattern when selecting. For example, if the top part of a pattern isn't selected, it won't be included in the movement. - **Straight**: This option selects everything within the designated distance, regardless of surface connections. ### Limit to Selected Patterns - Enabling "Limit to Selected Patterns" restricts movement and selection to only the selected pattern. This feature is crucial for precise adjustments. ## Workflows and Practical Applications Now, let's explore how this tool can be helpful in real-world scenarios. ### Simplifying Complex Adjustments For example, I have a twist top with a hole in the middle. Previously, I would need to use pins to align the fabric correctly, which could be tedious. With the advanced selection tool, I can simply select the area and move it through the hole without hassle. ### Efficient Knotting When tying a knot, I can easily adjust the fabric using the advanced pinching tool, allowing for a more streamlined process without needing multiple pins. ### Styling Options The advanced pinching tool also enhances styling capabilities. I can quickly tuck different parts of a shirt into jeans or adjust fit areas that may sit incorrectly. This feature dramatically speeds up the styling process and improves overall workflow. ## Conclusion Thank you for watching! If you have any questions, feel free to use the comment section below, and a clothing designer will respond. Don't forget to like and subscribe to our YouTube channel, where we have many great videos for you to explore. Keep having fun in Clo, and I’ll see you in the next video! Bye!
